mandatoryRules: Every file must receive an individual review record before any disposition decision.
Git ignored, hidden, backup, archive, worktree, cache-looking, generated-looking, dependency, binary and database files are included.
Directory name, filename, extension, Git ignore status, age, duplicate appearance or location may guide review but may never decide disposition by itself.
Every file is read byte-for-byte for SHA-256 and size verification.
Text-like files receive streamed content inspection for structural and domain signals.
Binary files receive magic/signature inspection plus cryptographic hash and metadata; specialist parsers are used in later phases where format-specific interpretation is required.
All Phase 16 dispositions remain UNDECIDED. Later phases may classify only with content evidence and provenance.
No delete, move, prune, truncate, reset, clean, garbage-collect or overwrite-for-cleanup action is permitted before Phase 100.
If a prior phase used bounded or pruned discovery, that evidence is navigation-only and cannot support deletion.
artifactRule: Review ledgers must be sharded below 20 MB; no generated file may exceed 25 MB.
